name: How to Read AC Installation Quotes in Los Angeles and Avoid Corner‑Cutting

mainEntity.name: What should I check on an AC installation quote in Los Angeles to avoid lowball offers that cut corners?
mainEntity.text: What should I check on an AC installation quote in Los Angeles to avoid lowball offers that cut corners?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lowball AC installation offers in Los Angeles often leave out critical steps or components you will later pay for separately. When comparing quotes, look first for a mention of Manual J or equivalent load calculations, rather than sizing based on square footage alone. Confirm that the price includes permits, any required HERS testing, and final inspections, not just “labor and materials.” Examine how ductwork is described. A vague line item like “connect to existing ducts” may not cover sealing, resizing, or replacing leaky runs that will fail inspections. Electrical work should specify whether new circuits, disconnects, or panel upgrades are included. Also check for clear details on condensate handling—proper drains, pumps if needed, and any code-required safety switches. Insist on written brand and model numbers for both condenser and air handler, plus thermostat type. Compare parts and labor warranty terms across bids, since short warranties can signal cheaper equipment or minimal support. If you see generic terms like “standard installation” without a detailed scope, ask for a revised itemized quote. Offers that seem dramatically cheaper often omit the very steps that ensure comfort, efficiency, and code compliance.
acceptedAnswer.description: To avoid lowball AC installation quotes in Los Angeles, check that Manual J load calculations, permits, HERS testing, ductwork scope, electrical upgrades, condensate handling, and brand/model numbers are clearly listed. Compare warranties, not just tonnage and SEER, and be wary of vague “standard installation” language without detailed line items.
